subsystems.name: Rotorcraft platform
subsystems.role: a dual-quadcopter that flies between sampling sites instead of staying put.

subsystems.name: Power source
subsystems.role: supplies electricity and warmth for years with no sunlight to rely on.

subsystems.name: Sample handling
subsystems.role: gets solid organics from the surface into the instruments without contaminating them.

subsystems.name: Chemical analyser
subsystems.role: the core instrument — separates and identifies organic molecules.

subsystems.name: Elemental mapper
subsystems.role: reads the bulk composition of the ground beneath the lander.

subsystems.name: Avionics and communications
subsystems.role: flies the craft and sends results directly back to Earth.
parts: X-band radio to the Deep Space Network

buildSteps.title: Pick the sites
buildSteps.detail: Radar and spectrometer maps from the Cassini orbiter (2004–2017) are used to find dune fields and impact craters where water ice and organics have mixed.

buildSteps.title: Exploit the environment
buildSteps.detail: Titan's atmosphere is about 1.5 bar and its gravity roughly one seventh of Earth's, so rotors can be smaller and turn slower than they would here — the design problem is doing it at 94 K.

buildSteps.title: Build the airframe
buildSteps.detail: Composite structures, eight rotors and the flight software are assembled and repeatedly drop- and flight-tested.

buildSteps.title: Build the instruments
buildSteps.detail: A gas chromatograph–mass spectrometer and a neutron/gamma-ray spectrometer are miniaturised, sealed and qualified for flight.

buildSteps.title: Fit power and thermal control
buildSteps.detail: A radioisotope generator is installed with insulation and plumbing that dumps waste heat where it is needed — the surrounding cold is both a problem and an advantage.

buildSteps.title: Qualify in chambers
buildSteps.detail: The whole craft is run in thermal-vacuum chambers under Titan-like cold and pressure, with the rotors spun in a dense simulated atmosphere.

buildSteps.title: Fly the cruise
buildSteps.detail: After launch the craft coasts for roughly six years, with gravity assists, kept alive and checked out by its own autonomous software.

buildSteps.title: Land under parachute
buildSteps.detail: Entry, descent and landing use a heat shield and parachute, followed by the first powered flight on Titan a short time later.

buildSteps.title: Hop and analyse
buildSteps.detail: Each flight of a few kilometres to tens of kilometres ends at a new site, where a sample is drilled, vaporised and analysed over hours or days before the next hop.

prerequisites.why: solar power is useless that far from the Sun, so the lander runs on the heat of decaying plutonium.
the Ingenuity helicopter proved powered flight on Mars from 2021, but Titan's air, cold and distance are a different problem.
instruments such as the Huygens gas chromatograph–mass spectrometer and later rover instruments already identify complex molecules in situ.
the Deep Space Network can receive the low data rates a direct radio link from Saturn's distance allows.
moving parts, seals and ovens must work reliably at 94 K without contaminating the very molecules being measured.

pathway.milestone: Cassini and Huygens data (2004–2017, with the Huygens landing in 2005) give maps of dunes, craters and polar lakes
pathway.unlocks: a shortlist of safe landing and sampling sites.

pathway.milestone: launch of the Dragonfly rotorcraft and arrival in the mid-2030s
pathway.unlocks: the first measurements of surface organics made on Titan itself, at many sites rather than one.

pathway.milestone: a mission that samples a polar lake liquid directly, by lander, float or submersible
pathway.unlocks: chemistry in a methane–ethane solvent, rather than in damp soil.
laboratory analysis on Earth — very hard to achieve, since an ascent vehicle must battle the thick atmosphere with weak gravity beneath it.
